note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with a new, severe, persistent headache with visual symptoms for three days, not fully relieved by usual analgesics; migraine is considered, with plan for in-person neurological and fundoscopic examination.

History:
- Presenting complaint: "Blinding" headache ongoing for three days, severe enough to interfere with work and daily activities.
- Onset/Durations/Progression:
  - Acute onset three days ago upon waking; continuous since then.
  - Prior headaches described as infrequent, brief, and responsive to Ibuprofen. Current headache is more severe and prolonged.
- Location: Generalized, but maximal over right eye.
- Severity: Rated 8/10 at worst, reduces to 5/10 after Ibuprofen, but never fully resolves.
- Exacerbating/Relieving Factors: 
  - Slight, temporary relief with Ibuprofen.
  - Worse with standing up quickly or certain head movements (stabbing pain, sensation of "something moving inside").
  - Light sensitivity (photophobia) present.
- Associated Symptoms:
  - Visual disturbances: "Shooting light," "weird kind of vision."
  - Mild nausea but no vomiting.
  - No fever, numbness, tingling, or focal weakness.
  - No changes in sense of taste or smell.
  - No sinus symptoms, no nosebleeds, no cough or sputum.
  - Reports tiredness, attributed to sleep disruption by headache.
  - Able to sleep at night, not woken by headache, but wakes with headache present.
- Systems Review/Pertinent Negatives:
  - No weight loss.
  - No history of similar severe headaches, migraines, or visual disturbances with past headaches.
  - No infectious symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- No significant chronic illnesses reported.
- No known drug allergies.
- Previous unexplained pain in childhood, resolved spontaneously.
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (brand/type not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented), started approximately one year ago. No side effects noted.
  - Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented), taken for current headache with partial relief.
- Blood pressure last checked a year ago at pharmacy, reported as normal.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Works from home; impaired ability to work due to headache (missed one full day, part of another, reduced productivity).
- Non-smoker.
- Drinks alcohol approximately once a week (quantity not specified).
- Denies illicit drug use.
- No recent travel abroad.

Family History:
- Mother has history of severe migraines with vomiting.
- No other relevant family history mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- No examination performed; virtual consultation only.
- No vital signs recorded.

Investigations:
- No new investigations performed or reviewed in this consult.
- Recent eye examination showed no vision change (timing not specified).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe headache (possible migraine, first severe episode)
  - Clinical impression: Likely migraine-type headache, but prolonged duration, visual disturbance, and incomplete response to analgesics warrant further evaluation.
  - Plan:
    - Book in-person appointment for full neurological and fundoscopic (back of eyes) examination and blood pressure check.
    - Start prescription of a stronger analgesic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); may take paracetamol concomitantly; to be taken with food.
    - Continue combined oral contraceptive for now; if confirmed migraine with aura (visual disturbance), will consider changing contraceptive agent.
    - Advised to seek immediate care at the Emergency Department if headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or changes in character before appointment.
    - Follow-up arrangement: Patient to book an appointment with support team for in-person assessment.

General plan items:
- Will review appropriateness of oral contraceptive at in-person evaluation, considering suspected migraine with aura.
- Will perform blood pressure check at next appointment.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):

● Missing but clinically expected elements for a consult:
  - No objective neurological or fundoscopic examination done (planned during follow-up).
  - No documentation of vital signs.
  - No complete medication reconciliation (contraceptive and Ibuprofen only; no details on OTC use, supplements, etc.).
  - No allergy status for non-drug substances recorded.
  - No detailed alcohol consumption (quantity per session not specified).
  - No detailed documentation of the specific contraceptive pill.
  - No lab or imaging investigations.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Audio interruptions (initial difficulty hearing patient).
  - At times, minor hesitation and unclear speech, but core clinical information present and comprehensible.
